transcript.text: Alright everyone, let's get started. As part of the normal production sign-off, I need to review the current draft stage plan with all of you before I can approve it. We've got the Atrium Theater booked for Friday, and the draft currently calls for a rotating platform, an overhead lift, floor anchors drilled into the stage, and a two-meter camera lane. Before I make my final approval decision, I need us to go through each of these elements together and make sure they're all compatible as one unified stage plan. Let's hear from technical, location, and movement staff — please walk me through any concerns or constraints you're seeing.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical compatibility issue before we go further. During a camera-rail test I ran, I confirmed that the rotating platform in the current draft would enter the rail's required three-meter exclusion lane. The technically approved layout is actually a fixed platform with a three-meter camera lane — not a rotating platform with a two-meter lane. I recorded this in the technical log, but I haven't yet updated Mara's design draft to reflect it. So the draft you're all looking at right now does not match the layout that passed technical testing.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical location constraint. I confirmed with the Atrium Theater's preservation officer this morning that drilling into the theater floor is prohibited. The approved replacement requires exactly 18 ballast bases for a freestanding platform. I have the written restriction, but it hasn't been added to the location packet yet, so none of you would have seen it. This directly conflicts with the current draft's call for floor anchors drilled into the stage.
transcript.speaker: A3

I reviewed the lead dancer's current medical clearance with the performer and choreographer, and it prohibits overhead lifts for this shoot. The cleared replacement is a floor duet. I have the signed clearance note, but I haven't yet entered the movement change in the rehearsal report, so none of you would have seen this. This directly conflicts with the current draft's call for an overhead lift.
